title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. - **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: What is Provisional Credit?
content:
When you file a dispute for a credit card transaction, you may hear the term "provisional credit" mentioned. We want to help you understand what this means and how it might apply to your situation.

## Understanding Provisional Credit

Provisional credit is a temporary credit that may be applied to your account while we investigate a disputed transaction. Think of it as Rho-Bank giving you the benefit of the doubt—we temporarily restore the disputed amount to your account so you're not out of pocket while we work to resolve the issue. This allows you to continue using your available credit without being impacted by charges that may ultimately be reversed.

## How It Works

If you're eligible for provisional credit and you file a dispute, the disputed amount will be temporarily credited back to your account, usually within a few business days of the dispute being filed. This credit remains on your account while our team investigates the dispute, which can take anywhere from a few days to several weeks depending on the complexity of the case.

## After the Investigation

Once the investigation is complete, one of two things will happen:

- **If the dispute is resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit becomes permanent, and the matter is closed. You won't owe anything for that transaction.
- **If the dispute is not resolved in your favor**: The provisional credit will be reversed, and the original charge will reappear on your account. You'll be responsible for paying the amount as part of your regular statement.

## Eligibility

Not all disputes automatically qualify for provisional credit. Eligibility depends on several factors, including your account history, the type of dispute, the amount in question, and other criteria. When you file a dispute with our customer service team, they will let you know whether provisional credit applies to your situation.

## Questions?

If you have questions about provisional credit or want to check on the status of a dispute you've filed, please contact our customer service team at 1-800-RHO-BANK or through the Rho-Bank mobile app. We're here to help guide you through the process and keep you informed every step of the way.

title: Moving Money Between Your Rho-Bank Accounts
content:
One of the many conveniences of being a Rho-Bank customer is the ability to easily move money between your accounts. Whether you're transferring funds from your checking account to your savings account to build up your emergency fund, moving money from savings to checking to cover an upcoming expense, or simply reorganizing your finances across multiple accounts, Rho-Bank makes it simple and straightforward.

## Self-Service Options

The fastest way to transfer money between your Rho-Bank accounts is through our digital banking platforms. Using the Rho-Bank mobile app or online banking at rhobank.com, you can initiate transfers instantly, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Simply log in, navigate to the transfer section, select your source and destination accounts, enter the amount, and confirm. It's that easy, and there's no fee for transferring money between your own Rho-Bank accounts.

## Need Assistance? We're Here to Help

If you prefer to have a customer service representative handle the transfer for you, or if you're having any trouble with the digital platforms, our team is happy to assist. Simply call us at 1-800-RHO-BANK or chat with us through the mobile app, and we can process the transfer on your behalf. This can be especially convenient if you're setting up a new savings account and want us to transfer the opening deposit from your checking account, or if you need to consolidate balances across multiple accounts.

## A Few Things to Keep in Mind

Both the source account (where the money is coming from) and the destination account (where the money is going) must be open and in good standing. The source account must have sufficient funds to cover the transfer amount—if the balance is too low, the transfer won't go through. Internal transfers between your own Rho-Bank accounts are always free of charge.

At Rho-Bank, we want managing your money to be as effortless as possible. If you have any questions about transferring funds or need any other assistance with your accounts, please don't hesitate to reach out. We're always here to help.

title: Moving Money Between Your Rho-Bank Accounts
content:
One of the many conveniences of being a Rho-Bank customer is the ability to easily move money between your accounts. Whether you're transferring funds from your checking account to your savings account to build up your emergency fund, moving money from savings to checking to cover an upcoming expense, or simply reorganizing your finances across multiple accounts, Rho-Bank makes it simple and straightforward.

## Self-Service Options

The fastest way to transfer money between your Rho-Bank accounts is through our digital banking platforms. Using the Rho-Bank mobile app or online banking at rhobank.com, you can initiate transfers instantly, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Simply log in, navigate to the transfer section, select your source and destination accounts, enter the amount, and confirm. It's that easy, and there's no fee for transferring money between your own Rho-Bank accounts.

## Need Assistance? We're Here to Help

If you prefer to have a customer service representative handle the transfer for you, or if you're having any trouble with the digital platforms, our team is happy to assist. Simply call us at 1-800-RHO-BANK or chat with us through the mobile app, and we can process the transfer on your behalf. This can be especially convenient if you're setting up a new savings account and want us to transfer the opening deposit from your checking account, or if you need to consolidate balances across multiple accounts.

## A Few Things to Keep in Mind

Both the source account (where the money is coming from) and the destination account (where the money is going) must be open and in good standing. The source account must have sufficient funds to cover the transfer amount—if the balance is too low, the transfer won't go through. Internal transfers between your own Rho-Bank accounts are always free of charge.

At Rho-Bank, we want managing your money to be as effortless as possible. If you have any questions about transferring funds or need any other assistance with your accounts, please don't hesitate to reach out. We're always here to help.

title: Moving Money Between Your Rho-Bank Accounts
content:
One of the many conveniences of being a Rho-Bank customer is the ability to easily move money between your accounts. Whether you're transferring funds from your checking account to your savings account to build up your emergency fund, moving money from savings to checking to cover an upcoming expense, or simply reorganizing your finances across multiple accounts, Rho-Bank makes it simple and straightforward.

## Self-Service Options

The fastest way to transfer money between your Rho-Bank accounts is through our digital banking platforms. Using the Rho-Bank mobile app or online banking at rhobank.com, you can initiate transfers instantly, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Simply log in, navigate to the transfer section, select your source and destination accounts, enter the amount, and confirm. It's that easy, and there's no fee for transferring money between your own Rho-Bank accounts.

## Need Assistance? We're Here to Help

If you prefer to have a customer service representative handle the transfer for you, or if you're having any trouble with the digital platforms, our team is happy to assist. Simply call us at 1-800-RHO-BANK or chat with us through the mobile app, and we can process the transfer on your behalf. This can be especially convenient if you're setting up a new savings account and want us to transfer the opening deposit from your checking account, or if you need to consolidate balances across multiple accounts.

## A Few Things to Keep in Mind

Both the source account (where the money is coming from) and the destination account (where the money is going) must be open and in good standing. The source account must have sufficient funds to cover the transfer amount—if the balance is too low, the transfer won't go through. Internal transfers between your own Rho-Bank accounts are always free of charge.

At Rho-Bank, we want managing your money to be as effortless as possible. If you have any questions about transferring funds or need any other assistance with your accounts, please don't hesitate to reach out. We're always here to help.

title: Moving Money Between Your Rho-Bank Accounts
content:
One of the many conveniences of being a Rho-Bank customer is the ability to easily move money between your accounts. Whether you're transferring funds from your checking account to your savings account to build up your emergency fund, moving money from savings to checking to cover an upcoming expense, or simply reorganizing your finances across multiple accounts, Rho-Bank makes it simple and straightforward.

## Self-Service Options

The fastest way to transfer money between your Rho-Bank accounts is through our digital banking platforms. Using the Rho-Bank mobile app or online banking at rhobank.com, you can initiate transfers instantly, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Simply log in, navigate to the transfer section, select your source and destination accounts, enter the amount, and confirm. It's that easy, and there's no fee for transferring money between your own Rho-Bank accounts.

## Need Assistance? We're Here to Help

If you prefer to have a customer service representative handle the transfer for you, or if you're having any trouble with the digital platforms, our team is happy to assist. Simply call us at 1-800-RHO-BANK or chat with us through the mobile app, and we can process the transfer on your behalf. This can be especially convenient if you're setting up a new savings account and want us to transfer the opening deposit from your checking account, or if you need to consolidate balances across multiple accounts.

## A Few Things to Keep in Mind

Both the source account (where the money is coming from) and the destination account (where the money is going) must be open and in good standing. The source account must have sufficient funds to cover the transfer amount—if the balance is too low, the transfer won't go through. Internal transfers between your own Rho-Bank accounts are always free of charge.

At Rho-Bank, we want managing your money to be as effortless as possible. If you have any questions about transferring funds or need any other assistance with your accounts, please don't hesitate to reach out. We're always here to help.
